newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Black Sea Shipping Co profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Black Sea Shipping Co profits fall.

text.p: Ukraine's state-owned Black Sea Shipping Company on Monday reported a drop in net profits for the first nine months of the year to 15.9 million hryvnias from 20.7 million hryvnias in the same 1995 period.
The company said in a statement passed to the transport ministry that it had sold 28 ships this year for scrap, mostly to Indian firms, and another 50 vessels would be sold by 2000.
Vice-President Anatoly Antonov, said last week that the company was having big financial problems because of a fall in scrap metal and cargo prices.
About 90 percent of the vessels belonging to what was once the Soviet Union's biggest and most prestigious shipping company work abroad, transporting goods for foreign firms.
The firm ran into trouble after the Soviet Union collapsed and has been forced to raise funds by selling off parts of its ageing fleet, which stood at 191 vessels in early December.
Company officials said potential customers often refused to use ships more than 15 years old, while the average age of their fleet was 20 to 22 years old.
Transport Minister Ivan Dankevych said in October that the company had reduced its debts by $60 million and managed to free about 25 ships impounded in foreign ports for unpaid bills.
Statistics issued in May showed the company owed $228 million to foreign creditors and $38 million to Ukrainian firms and in turn was owed $103 million by Russian debtors.
The government is considering a share issue but there are no plans to privatise the company next year.
The company owed its workers 12 million hryvnias at the start of December, transport ministry figures showed.
In the first nine months of the year 59 ships were arrested and $28 million was spent freeing ships.
